Navigates to the new job's show page directly (rather than # notifying the parent to decide) — a redirect issued from a parent's # `handle_info` in reaction to a component message lands one message # round-trip too late for `Phoenix.LiveViewTest.render_submit/1` to # observe it as a live redirect, which the board's own spex relies on. def handle_event("save", %{"job" => params}, socket) do {pay_rate_input, params} = split_pay_params(params) socket = assign(socket, :pay_rate_input, pay_rate_input) case Scheduling.create_job(socket.assigns.current_scope, params) do {:ok, job} -> {:noreply, push_navigate(socket, to: ~p"/schedule/jobs/#{job.id}")} {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, to_form(changeset, as: :job))} end end def handle_event("save", %{"assignment" => %{"cleaner_id" => cleaner_id}}, socket) do case Scheduling.assign_cleaner( socket.assigns.current_scope, socket.assigns.job, parse_id(cleaner_id) ) do {:ok, job} -> notify_parent({:saved, job}) {:noreply, assign(socket, :conflict_error, nil)} {:error, :unavailable} -> {:noreply, assign( socket, :conflict_error, "This assignment has a scheduling conflict: the cleaner is unavailable that day." )} {:error, :overlap} -> {:noreply, assign( socket, :conflict_error, "This assignment was rejected: it overlaps another booking for this cleaner." )} end end defp parse_id(""), do: nil defp parse_id(nil), do: nil defp parse_id(id) when is_binary(id), do: String.to_integer(id) defp parse_id(id) when is_integer(id), do: id defp notify_parent(msg), do: send(self(), {__MODULE__, msg}) defp list_properties(%{active_account_id: account_id}) do Property |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id) |> order_by([p], asc: p.service_address) |> Repo.all() end defp property_options(properties), do: Enum.map(properties, &{&1.service_address, &1.id}) defp cleaner_options(cleaners), do: Enum.map(cleaners, &{&1.name || &1.email, &1.id}) defp pay_type_options, do: [{"Hourly", "hourly"}, {"Piece rate", "piece_rate"}] defp pay_type_value(form) do case form[:pay_type].value do nil -> "" value -> to_string(value) end end # defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story843.Criterion7190Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 843 — Get loud, acknowledged alerts when my schedule changes
  Criterion 7190 — Moving a job's time on the schedule board pushes the
  reassigned cleaner a notification describing the old and new times.

  Assumes the board exposes a per-job start-time control
  (`[data-test='job-<id>-start-time-input']`, `phx-change="reschedule_job"`)
  alongside the cleaner-select control already assumed by story 834's
  criterion 7170.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "a moved job notifies the assigned cleaner" do
    scenario "moved job notifies the cleaner" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "I am a cleaner with a job scheduled today at 1:00 PM", context do
        cleaner =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "cleaner-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        cleaner_conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn(), cleaner)
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
            scheduled_date: Date.utc_today(),
            start_time: ~T[13:00:00],
            end_time: ~T[14:30:00]
          })

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{cleaner: cleaner, cleaner_conn: cleaner_conn, job: job})}
      end

      when_ "the office moves that job to 3:00 PM", context do
        {:ok, board_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule")

        board_live
        |> element("[data-test='job-#{context.job.id}-start-time-input']")
        |> render_change(%{"start_time" => "15:00"})

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "I receive a notification describing the change from 1:00 PM to 3:00 PM", context do
        {:ok, today_live, html} = live(context.cleaner_conn, ~p"/field")

        assert has_element?(today_live, "[data-test='schedule-alert']")
        assert html =~ "1:00 PM"
        assert html =~ "3:00 PM"

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.JobFormComponentTest do
  use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true

  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest
  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  import CleanerCrm.ClientsFixtures
  import CleanerCrm.SchedulingFixtures

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.JobFormComponent

  # Hosts the component in isolation (no router route required), same
  # pattern as ClientLive.PropertyFormComponentTest. Forwards the
  # component's parent notification to the test process so assertions
  # can use `assert_receive`.
  defmodule Host do
    use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view

    @impl true
    def mount(_params, session, socket) do
      {:ok,
       assign(socket, %{
         test_pid: session["test_pid"],
         current_scope: session["scope"],
         action: session["action"],
         job: session["job"]
       })}
    end

    @impl true
    def render(assigns) do
      ~H"""
      <.live_component
        module={JobFormComponent}
        id="job-form"
        current_scope={@current_scope}
        action={@action}
        job={@job}
      />
      """
    end

    @impl true
    def handle_info({JobFormComponent, _} = message, socket) do
      send(socket.assigns.test_pid, message)
      {:noreply, socket}
    end
  end

  defp scope_fixture do
    user = user_fixture()
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)

    {:ok, account} =
      Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})

    %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
  end

  defp render_host(session) do
    session = Map.put(session, "test_pid", self())
    live_isolated(build_conn(), Host, session: session)
  end

  describe "creating a job" do
    test "renders the job form with the account's properties" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Jamie Rivera"})
      property_fixture(scope, client, %{service_address: "12 Oak Lane"})

      {:ok, _lv, html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "job" => %Job{}})

      assert html =~ "12 Oak Lane"
      assert html =~ "job-form"
    end

    test "creates an unassigned job and navigates to its show page" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "job" => %Job{}})

      {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
        lv
        |> form("[data-test='job-form']",
          job: %{
            property_id: property.id,
            date: Date.to_iso8601(Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 14)),
            start_time: "09:00",
            end_time: "11:00"
          }
        )
        |> render_submit()

      job_id = path |> String.split("/") |> List.last()
      job = Scheduling.get_job!(scope, job_id)

      assert job.property_id == property.id
      assert job.cleaner_id == nil
      assert job.start_time == ~T[09:00:00]
    end

    test "creates a job pre-assigned to a cleaner" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)
      cleaner = cleaner_fixture(scope, scope.active_account)

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "job" => %Job{}})

      {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
        lv
        |> form("[data-test='job-form']",
          job: %{
            property_id: property.id,
            cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
            date: Date.to_iso8601(Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 14)),
            start_time: "10:00",
            end_time: "12:00"
          }
        )
        |> render_submit()

      job_id = path |> String.split("/") |> List.last()
      job = Scheduling.get_job!(scope, job_id)

      assert job.cleaner_id == cleaner.id
    end

    test "creates a job with hourly pay for the assigned cleaner" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)
      cleaner = cleaner_fixture(scope, scope.active_account)

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "job" => %Job{}})

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='job-form']", job: %{pay_type: "hourly"})
      |> render_change()

      {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
        lv
        |> form("[data-test='job-form']",
          job: %{
            property_id: property.id,
            cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
            date: Date.to_iso8601(Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 14)),
            start_time: "09:00",
            end_time: "11:00",
            pay_type: "hourly",
            hourly_rate: "25.00"
          }
        )
        |> render_submit()

      job_id = path |> String.split("/") |> List.last()
      job = Scheduling.get_job!(scope, job_id)

      assert job.pay_type == :hourly
      assert job.hourly_rate_cents == 2500
      assert job.piece_rate_cents == nil
    end

    test "creates a job with piece-rate pay" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "job" => %Job{}})

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='job-form']", job: %{pay_type: "piece_rate"})
      |> render_change()

      {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
        lv
        |> form("[data-test='job-form']",
          job: %{
            property_id: property.id,
            date: Date.to_iso8601(Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 14)),
            start_time: "09:00",
            end_time: "11:00",
            pay_type: "piece_rate",
            piece_rate: "80.00"
          }
        )
        |> render_submit()

      job_id = path |> String.split("/") |> List.last()
      job = Scheduling.get_job!(scope, job_id)

      assert job.pay_type == :piece_rate
      assert job.piece_rate_cents == 8000
      assert job.hourly_rate_cents == nil
    end

    test "rejects a submission missing the required date" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :new, "job" => %Job{}})

      html =
        lv
        |> form("[data-test='job-form']",
          job: %{property_id: property.id, date: "", start_time: "09:00", end_time: "11:00"}
        )
        |> render_submit()

      assert has_element?(lv, "[data-test='job-form']")
      assert html =~ "can't be blank" or html =~ "is required"
    end
  end

  describe "assigning a cleaner to an existing job" do
    test "renders the assignment form" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)
      job = job_fixture(scope, property)

      {:ok, _lv, html} = render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :assign, "job" => job})

      assert html =~ "assignment-form"
    end

    test "assigns the cleaner when there is no conflict" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)
      cleaner = cleaner_fixture(scope, scope.active_account)

      job =
        job_fixture(scope, property, %{
          scheduled_date: next_tuesday(),
          start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
          end_time: ~T[11:00:00]
        })

      {:ok, lv, _html} = render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :assign, "job" => job})

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='assignment-form']", assignment: %{cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
      |> render_submit()

      assert_receive {JobFormComponent, {:saved, %Job{} = updated}}
      assert updated.cleaner_id == cleaner.id
    end

    test "rejects the assignment when the cleaner has a time-off block that day" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)
      cleaner = cleaner_fixture(scope, scope.active_account)
      friday = next_friday()

      availability_block_fixture(scope, cleaner, %{date: friday, all_day: true})

      job =
        job_fixture(scope, property, %{
          scheduled_date: friday,
          start_time: ~T[10:00:00],
          end_time: ~T[12:00:00]
        })

      {:ok, lv, _html} = render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :assign, "job" => job})

      html =
        lv
        |> form("[data-test='assignment-form']", assignment: %{cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
        |> render_submit()

      assert html =~ "conflict"
      assert html =~ "unavailable"
      refute_receive {JobFormComponent, {:saved, _}}
    end

    test "rejects the assignment when it overlaps another booking for that cleaner" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)
      cleaner = cleaner_fixture(scope, scope.active_account)
      booking_date = Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 14)

      job_fixture(scope, property, %{
        cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
        scheduled_date: booking_date,
        start_time: ~T[10:00:00],
        end_time: ~T[12:00:00]
      })

      second_job =
        job_fixture(scope, property, %{
          scheduled_date: booking_date,
          start_time: ~T[11:00:00],
          end_time: ~T[13:00:00]
        })

      {:ok, lv, _html} =
        render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :assign, "job" => second_job})

      html =
        lv
        |> form("[data-test='assignment-form']", assignment: %{cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
        |> render_submit()

      assert html =~ "overlap"
      refute_receive {JobFormComponent, {:saved, _}}
    end
  end

  describe "editing an existing job" do
    test "sets pay type and rate on a job that had none" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      client = client_fixture(scope)
      property = property_fixture(scope, client)
      job = job_fixture(scope, property)

      {:ok, lv, _html} = render_host(%{"scope" => scope, "action" => :edit, "job" => job})

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='job-form']", job: %{pay_type: "hourly"})
      |> render_change()

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='job-form']",
        job: %{
          date: Date.to_iso8601(job.scheduled_date),
          start_time: "09:00",
          end_time: "11:00",
          pay_type: "hourly",
          hourly_rate: "20.00"
        }
      )
      |> render_submit()

      assert_receive {JobFormComponent, {:job_updated, %Job{} = updated}}
      assert updated.pay_type == :hourly
      assert updated.hourly_rate_cents == 2000
    end
  end

  defp next_tuesday do
    today = Date.utc_today()
    offset = Integer.mod(2 - Date.day_of_week(today) - 1, 7) + 1
    Date.add(today, offset + 7)
  end

    today = Date.utc_today()

    Date.add(today, offset + 7)
  end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Notifications do
  @moduledoc """
  Client appointment reminders with confirm/reschedule actions, and
  cleaner schedule-change alerts requiring explicit acknowledgment with
  office visibility into what's still unacknowledged. Email/SMS
  delivery is abstracted behind `CleanerCrm.Notifications.Delivery`.

  Most functions are scoped by the caller's `Scope`. The confirm,
  reschedule, and delivery-status webhook endpoints are reached by an
  unauthenticated client or provider, so they look a notification up by
  its opaque `token` (or the provider's message id) instead.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  alias CleanerCrm.Notifications.{
    Notification,
    ReminderNotifier,
    ReminderScheduler,
    ReminderSettings
  }

  ## Reminder settings

  @doc "The account's reminder settings, defaulting to a 24-hour lead time if never configured."
  def get_reminder_settings(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(ReminderSettings, account_id: account_id) do
      nil -> %ReminderSettings{account_id: account_id}
      settings -> settings
    end
  end

  def change_reminder_settings(%Scope{} = scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    scope |> get_reminder_settings() |> ReminderSettings.changeset(attrs)
  end

  def update_reminder_settings(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> get_reminder_settings()
    |> ReminderSettings.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert_or_update()
  end

  @doc "Runs the periodic reminder scan now — see `CleanerCrm.Notifications.ReminderScheduler`."
  defdelegate send_due_reminders(), to: ReminderScheduler, as: :scan_and_send

  ## Notifications

  def create_notification(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Notification{account_id: account_id}
    |> Notification.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc "The office's delivery log: every notification for the account, most recent first."
  def list_notifications(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Notification
    |> where([n], n.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([n], desc: n.inserted_at)
    |> preload([:client, :cleaner])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  ## Public confirm/reschedule — reached by token, no scope available

  def get_notification_by_token(token) when is_binary(token) do
    Repo.get_by(Notification, token: token)
  end

  def confirm_reminder(token) when is_binary(token) do
    with %Notification{} = notification <- get_notification_by_token(token) do
      update_status(notification, status: :confirmed, confirmed_at: DateTime.utc_now())
    else
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
    end
  end

  def request_reschedule(token) when is_binary(token) do
    with %Notification{} = notification <- get_notification_by_token(token) do
      update_status(notification,
        status: :reschedule_requested,
        reschedule_requested_at: DateTime.utc_now()
      )
    else
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
    end
  end

  @doc "True once the client has confirmed the most recent reminder sent for this job."
  def job_confirmed?(job_id) do
    Notification
    |> where([n], n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :reminder and n.status == :confirmed)
    |> Repo.exists?()
  end

  @doc "True once the client has asked to reschedule via the most recent reminder for this job."
  def reschedule_requested?(job_id) do
    Notification
    |> where(
      [n],
      n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :reminder and n.status == :reschedule_requested
    )
    |> Repo.exists?()
  end

  @doc """
  The client's confirm/reschedule decision on their most recent
  reminder for this job, for `ScheduleLive.Index` to render on the
  board — `nil` (no decision yet), `:confirmed`, or
  `:reschedule_requested`.
  """
  def reminder_status_for_job(job_id) do
    Notification
    |> where([n], n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :reminder)
    |> where([n], n.status in [:confirmed, :reschedule_requested])
    |> order_by([n], desc: n.inserted_at)
    |> limit(1)
    |> select([n], n.status)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  ## Twilio delivery-status webhook

  @doc """
  Applies a Twilio status callback: marks the matching notification
  delivered or undelivered, and — for an undeliverable SMS reminder —
  falls back to emailing the client and flags it for office visibility.
  """
  def handle_delivery_status(%{"MessageSid" => sid, "MessageStatus" => status} = params)
      when is_binary(sid) do
    # Most-recent match: real SIDs are unique, but webhook retries racing
    # inserts (or duplicated test data) must not 500 the endpoint.
    notification =
      from(n in Notification,
        where: n.provider_message_id == ^sid,
        order_by: [desc: n.inserted_at],
        limit: 1
      )
      |> Repo.one()

    case notification do
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
      notification -> apply_delivery_status(notification, status, params["ErrorCode"])
    end
  end

  def handle_delivery_status(_params), do: {:error, :invalid_payload}

  defp apply_delivery_status(notification, "delivered", _error_code) do
    update_status(notification, status: :delivered, delivered_at: DateTime.utc_now())
  end

  defp apply_delivery_status(notification, status, error_code)
       when status in ["failed", "undelivered"] do
    with {:ok, updated} <-
           update_status(notification, status: :undelivered, failure_reason: error_code || status) do
      maybe_fallback_to_email(updated)
      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  defp apply_delivery_status(notification, _status, _error_code), do: {:ok, notification}

  defp maybe_fallback_to_email(
         %Notification{kind: :reminder, channel: :sms, client_id: client_id} = notification
       )
       when not is_nil(client_id) do
    client = Repo.get!(CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, notification.client_id)
    job = Repo.get!(CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job, notification.job_id)
    token = generate_token()

    confirm_url = reminder_url("/reminders/confirm/#{token}")
    reschedule_url = reminder_url("/reminders/reschedule/#{token}")

    {:ok, _email} = ReminderNotifier.deliver_reminder(client, job, confirm_url, reschedule_url)

    %Notification{account_id: notification.account_id}
    |> Notification.changeset(%{
      client_id: client.id,
      job_id: job.id,
      kind: :reminder,
      channel: :email,
      status: :sent,
      token: token,
      sent_at: DateTime.utc_now()
    })
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  defp maybe_fallback_to_email(_notification), do: :ok

  ## Schedule-change alerts (story 843 groundwork)

  def acknowledge(token) when is_binary(token) do
    with %Notification{} = notification <- get_notification_by_token(token) do
      update_status(notification, status: :acknowledged, acknowledged_at: DateTime.utc_now())
    else
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
    end
  end

  @doc "Pending schedule-change alerts a cleaner hasn't acknowledged yet, for office visibility."
  def list_unacknowledged(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Notification
    |> where(
      [n],
      n.account_id == ^account_id and n.kind == :schedule_change and n.status == :pending
    )
    |> preload([:cleaner, :job])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Job ids whose most recent schedule-change notification hasn't been
  acknowledged (`:pending` or `:escalated`) — for `ScheduleLive.Index`
  to keep a cancelled job's row (and its ack-status/channel
  indicators) on the board until the office has visibility into it,
  per story 843's escalation path. A job with no schedule-change
  notification at all, or whose latest one is already `:acknowledged`,
  is left out.
  """
  def job_ids_with_unacknowledged_schedule_change(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id})
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Notification
    |> where([n], n.account_id == ^account_id and n.kind == :schedule_change)
    |> distinct([n], n.job_id)
    |> order_by([n], asc: n.job_id, desc: n.inserted_at)
    |> select([n], {n.job_id, n.status})
    |> Repo.all()
    |> Enum.filter(fn {_job_id, status} -> status != :acknowledged end)
    |> Enum.map(fn {job_id, _status} -> job_id end)
  end

  @doc """
  The most recent schedule-change alert pushed for this job — `nil`,
  or a `Notification` exposing `:status`
  (`:pending` | `:acknowledged` | `:escalated`) and `:channel`
  (`:push` | `:sms` | `:email`). This is the contract
  `CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.Index` reads defensively to show a job's
  ack status on the board.
  """
  def latest_schedule_change_for_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, job_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Notification
    |> where(
      [n],
      n.account_id == ^account_id and n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :schedule_change
    )
    |> order_by([n], desc: n.inserted_at)
    |> limit(1)
    |> Repo.one()
    |> maybe_escalate()
  end

  # A same-day change nobody has acknowledged within the escalation
  # window re-sends via the fallback channel (SMS) and flags as
  # escalated for office visibility. Computed on read rather than a
  # separate periodic pass — every read of a job's alert (the board,
  # `FieldLive.Today`) goes through here, so none of them can show a
  # stale "pending" past the window.
  @escalation_window_seconds 600

  defp maybe_escalate(%Notification{status: :pending} = notification) do
    if escalation_due?(notification) do
      {:ok, updated} =
        update_status(notification,
          status: :escalated,
          channel: :sms,
          escalated_at: DateTime.utc_now()
        )

      updated
    else
      notification
    end
  end

  defp maybe_escalate(notification), do: notification

  defp escalation_due?(%Notification{pushed_at: nil}), do: false

  defp escalation_due?(%Notification{pushed_at: pushed_at, job_id: job_id}) do

    Date.compare(job.scheduled_date, Date.utc_today()) != :gt and
      DateTime.diff(DateTime.utc_now(), pushed_at, :second) >= @escalation_window_seconds
  end

  defp update_status(%Notification{} = notification, attrs) do

  @moduledoc """
  Recurring plans and the jobs they generate, cleaner time-off, and
  conflict-aware assignment.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Property
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo

  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.{
    AvailabilityBlock,
    ConflictDetector,
    Job,
    Recurrence,
    RecurringPlan
  }

  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  ## Jobs

  def get_job!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Job
    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_job(%Scope{}, %Job{} = job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Job.changeset(job, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Creates a job. Recorded in the audit trail as authored by the
  caller, unless `actor: :system` is passed — used when the job is one
  occurrence materialized from a recurring plan rather than a job a
  human directly asked for (see `create_recurring_plan/2`).
  """
  def create_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs, opts \\ [])
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, job} <-
           %Job{account_id: account_id}
           |> Job.changeset(derive_client_id(account_id, attrs))
           |> Repo.insert() do
      record_job_created(scope, job, Keyword.get(opts, :actor, :user))
      {:ok, job}
    end
  end

  # The board's own job form (and a recurring plan's own materialized
  # occurrences, via `Recurrence.job_attrs/1`) only ever carry a
  # `property_id` — never a `client_id` — so a job created either way
  # otherwise saves with `client_id: nil`. That breaks anything reading
  # the client straight off the job rather than through its property
  # (story 836's invoicing does both a card-on-file charge lookup and
  # the invoice's own client label this way), so every job creation
  # backfills `client_id` from its property here rather than requiring
  # every caller to remember to. A caller that already supplies a
  # `client_id` (fixtures with only a client on hand, no property) is
  # left alone.
  defp derive_client_id(account_id, attrs) do
    if blank?(fetch_attr(attrs, :client_id)) do
      case fetch_attr(attrs, :property_id) do
        value when value in [nil, ""] -> attrs
        property_id -> put_client_id_from_property(attrs, account_id, property_id)
      end
    else
      attrs
    end
  end

  defp put_client_id_from_property(attrs, account_id, property_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(Property, id: property_id, account_id: account_id) do
      %Property{client_id: client_id} when not is_nil(client_id) ->
        # Match whichever key style (atom or string) `attrs` already
        # uses — `Ecto.Changeset.cast/4` raises on a map mixing both.
        if Map.has_key?(attrs, :property_id) do
          Map.put(attrs, :client_id, client_id)
        else
          Map.put(attrs, "client_id", client_id)
        end

      _ ->
        attrs
    end
  end

  defp fetch_attr(attrs, key), do: Map.get(attrs, key) || Map.get(attrs, to_string(key))

  defp blank?(nil), do: true
  defp blank?(""), do: true
  defp blank?(_value), do: false

  defp record_job_created(scope, job, :system) do
    Recorder.record_system(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, job_created_values(job))
  end

  defp record_job_created(scope, job, :user) do
    Recorder.record(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, job_created_values(job))
  end

  # Deliberately omits `scheduled_date`: a "created" entry's own
  # subject label (job → property/client) is enough to identify which
  # job this is, and surfacing it here would read as a schedule change
  # (`field_changes/1`'s "Scheduled date: ..." line) indistinguishable
  # from an actual reschedule recorded later by `update_job/3`.
  defp job_created_values(job) do
    %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id}
  end

  @doc """
  Lists every job scheduled between `week_start` and six days later,
  cleaner/property/client preloaded, ordered for the board.
  """
  def list_jobs_for_week(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Date{} = week_start)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    week_end = Date.add(week_start, 6)

    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.scheduled_date >= ^week_start and
        j.scheduled_date <= ^week_end and j.status != :cancelled
    )
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Lists every non-cancelled job for the account, cleaner/property/client
  preloaded, ordered for the board. Unlike `list_jobs_for_week/2`, this
  isn't bounded to a single week — a recurring plan's series can span
  months, and the board needs to account for all of it at a glance.

  `:include_cancelled_ids` (default `[]`) admits specific cancelled
  jobs back in anyway — the board's own escape hatch for a cancelled
  job that still carries an unacknowledged schedule-change
  notification (story 843): the office needs to keep seeing its
  ack-status until the cleaner acknowledges, and the escalation check
  needs the job rendered at all to ever run. Other callers passing no
  opts see the same non-cancelled set as before.
  """
  def list_jobs(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, opts \\ [])
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    include_cancelled_ids = Keyword.get(opts, :include_cancelled_ids, [])

    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and
        (j.status != :cancelled or j.id in ^include_cancelled_ids)
    )
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Assigns (or reassigns) a job to a cleaner, rejecting the move with
  `{:error, :unavailable}` or `{:error, :overlap}` when it conflicts
  with that cleaner's time off or an existing booking. A `nil`
  `cleaner_id` always succeeds (unassigning never conflicts).
  """
  def assign_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <-
           ConflictDetector.check_assignment(
             scope,
             cleaner_id,
             job.scheduled_date,
             job.start_time,
             job.end_time,
             exclude_job_id: job.id
           ),
         {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{cleaner_id: cleaner_id}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_reassigned",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id},
        %{"cleaner_id" => cleaner_id}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  def cancel_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :cancelled}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_cancelled",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
        %{"status" => "cancelled"}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Updates a job's schedule and/or price — a reschedule, a price
  change, or both, made directly from the board rather than through
  `assign_cleaner/3`'s conflict-checked path. Records only the fields
  that actually changed to the audit trail, attributed to the caller.
  """
  def update_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    changeset = Job.changeset(job, derive_client_id(account_id, attrs))

    with {:ok, updated} <- Repo.update(changeset) do
      record_job_updated(scope, job, changeset, updated)
      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  @audited_update_fields ~w(scheduled_date start_time end_time agreed_price_cents status)a

  defp record_job_updated(scope, job, changeset, updated) do
    changed_fields =
      changeset.changes
      |> Map.keys()
      |> Enum.filter(&(&1 in @audited_update_fields))

    if changed_fields != [] do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        update_action(changed_fields),
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        audit_snapshot(job, changed_fields),
        audit_snapshot(updated, changed_fields)
      )
    end
  end

  defp update_action(changed_fields) do
    cond do
      Enum.any?(changed_fields, &(&1 in [:scheduled_date, :start_time, :end_time])) ->
        "job_rescheduled"

      :agreed_price_cents in changed_fields ->
        "job_price_changed"

      true ->
        "job_updated"
    end
  end

  end
